ratings.why: Exact @Scribe is stated, but case and boundary variants are a real choice a careful builder settles and tells the customer about.
Calling the agent and replying to every ordinary message would be a plain defect anyone would report.
The request says Shift+Enter inserts a newline; also sending a half-written draft breaks the stated behaviour.
Calling the agent with no visible, correctly attributed reply makes the core feature useless.
If an HTTP error or network failure is not treated as a failure, the working state hangs and the required alert and Retry never appear.
Clearing stale alerts and keeping one Retry tied to the right message is careful handling, but it costs less than the main failure path.
A retry that sends the draft or the wrong message produces a reply to text Maya never sent there.
Duplicate sends from a double click are a real but smaller cost that a careful builder guards against.
Keeping the composer usable and replies in order while one is pending is careful handling of a likely situation.
A working status left up after the reply or alert contradicts what is shown and misleads screen-reader users.
Which characters count as whitespace and whether the draft is kept is a small choice worth keeping the same in the client and the endpoint.
Disabling Send or leaving it active is a matter of taste, since either way the text is ignored as asked.
Echoing exactly depends on what the sent text is, so trimming must be the same in the display, the POST and the reply and should be stated.
Malformed bodies come only from hand calls, but a crash or hang there is a real cost a careful builder avoids.
A JSON content type and a parseable 400 body keep the front end and tests reliable and are cheap to get right.
How other methods and unknown paths are answered on a local demo app is polish the request does not need.
A static handler that leaks source or arbitrary files through traversal is a real security cost even for a local app.
Binding only to localhost matches a local app, and exposing it on shared networks is a real but modest risk.
Node's default error for a busy port is good enough for a small local app.
Reading message text as HTML loses typed text and lets content run script, a plain defect.
A reload on send could drop the session transcript or abandon the agent call, breaking the feature.
The request allows session state, so a careful builder picks a store and says what survives a reload.
The fixture must start empty reliably and not disturb the seeded room, or testers get confusing results.
Guidance left over a real conversation is clutter, a small but real cost.
Starting light with a matching label is a fine reading of the request, and following the system theme is taste.
The request requires the toggle to switch back, and a label or appearance that sticks after repeated toggles is a plain defect.
A visible button and usable narrow layouts are both stated, so a toggle hidden at 320px breaks the request.
Low contrast or invisible focus in dark mode is a real usability cost a careful builder checks.
A pasted long URL pushing the page sideways breaks the stated rule of no page-level horizontal scrolling.
Scrolling to the newest message is expected chat behaviour, and missing it is a smaller cost.
Returning focus to the textbox after clicking Send is a convenience, not something the request depends on.
Announcing the arrived reply completes the accessible waiting experience the request starts with role status.
Seeded times in the future or in an odd format read as broken, so a sensible time display is careful work.
New messages landing anywhere but after the seed in send order would be a plain defect in a conversation.
Size limits on a local single-user demo are speculative hardening.
IME composition and mobile newlines are edge cases beyond this English-language local demo.
The next maintainer needs the one test command and Node version, which is cheap to state.
The request requires Scribe to be clearly identified as a demonstration agent, so hidden or person-like identity fails it.
The request asks for a realistic seed, and placeholder text weakens the demo at a modest cost.
The current user is Maya, so composed messages attributed to anyone else would mislead.
